definitions.explanation: A feeling of resentment toward someone because of their advantages, possessions, or relationships.

examples.japanese: {嫉妬|しっと}に{燃|も}えている。
{彼女|かのじょ}の{成功|せいこう}に{嫉妬|しっと}した。
examples.english: I felt jealous of her success.

examples.japanese: {嫉妬深|しっとぶか}い{人|ひと}だ。
{友達|ともだち}が{新|あたら}しい{車|くるま}を{買|か}ったと{聞|き}いて、{嫉妬|しっと}してしまった。
examples.english: When I heard my friend bought a new car, I couldn't help feeling jealous.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}が{他|ほか}の{女性|じょせい}と{話|はな}しているのを{見|み}て、{嫉妬|しっと}を{感|かん}じた。
examples.english: I felt jealous seeing him talking to another woman.

notes:
{嫉妬|しっと} often implies jealousy in romantic contexts but can also mean envy of others' success.

RELATED WORDS:
- {嫉妬|しっと}する: to be jealous (verb)
- {嫉妬深|しっとぶか}い: jealous (personality)
- {羨望|せんぼう} (せんぼう): envy (more literary)
- やきもち: jealousy (colloquial, especially romantic)

NUANCE:
{嫉妬|しっと} tends to be stronger and more negative than simply being envious.
